factors.input_timing: revtq, cshprq from m_QCompustat: time_avail_m = max(datadate+3mo, rdq month) with >6-month-late filers dropped (CompustatQuarterly.py L83-113) — a quarter announced mid-month t is first usable at t, satisfying end-of-month-t availability; all comparison terms are calendar lags t-3..t-24 of that already-lagged series.
factors.mechanism: Script uses backward calendar merges (time_avail_m - 3..24 months, RevenueSurprise.py L49-87); engine _op_seasonal_surprise_zscore L1130-1154 uses backward shifts on the contiguous grid — no self-join aligns t with t+k. Caveats (not construction leaks): missing-rdq rows fall back to the datadate+3 assumption, and Compustat FUNDQ is not point-in-time so restated values can overwrite originals — an upstream vintage limitation shared by the whole OSAP pipeline, and the dedup 'keep latest datadate' only ever selects among rows whose own availability stamp is <= the month.

factors.input_timing: ni and ceq from the same m_aCompustat row at t, i.e. the latest annual report with datadate >=6 months before t (verified 6-month lag + 12-month forward fill).
factors.mechanism: Same-month division of two co-stamped, already-lagged annual fields on both sides (script RoE.py L31; engine div node on m_aCompustat panels); dedup differences (script keep-first vs engine pivot keep-last) choose among rows all available at t.

factors.input_timing: sale from m_aCompustat at t (>=6-month-lagged annual filing); mve_permco from monthlyCRSP/SMT at t = end-of-month-t price x shares, public at end of t.
factors.mechanism: Numerator is stale-by-construction accounting data, denominator is contemporaneous month-t market equity used at its own availability month — standard OSAP convention, no future field on either side (script SP.py L40; engine div node).

factors.input_timing: monthlyCRSP ret: the return over month t, stamped time_avail_m = t (CRSPMonthly.py L73), fully realized at end of t. Script uses ret_t at t; engine tree lags it so the engine value at t is ret_{t-1}.
factors.mechanism: Script (fill_null(0) of ret_t, no lead) uses exactly end-of-month-t information; engine's lag(ret,1) (spec tree + _op_lag) uses month t-1 — one month *staler* than the script (reconciliation-confirmed 'timing_lag_shift' discrepancy) but strictly backward, so neither side sees future data.

factors.input_timing: shrout and cfacshr from monthlyCRSP at months t-6 and t-18 (script: calendar merges on time_avail_m - 6/18, ShareIss1Y.py L59-74; engine: time_lagged_value = backward shift on contiguous grid). Both reference months precede t.
factors.mechanism: cfacshr is cumulative-to-snapshot, but the signal is a ratio of adjusted shares at two past dates, so the snapshot component cancels and only splits between t-18 and t-6 (all pre-t events) enter — matching the no-lookahead analysis cited in the script header (OSAP issue #152); all joins are t-minus-k merges, never t-plus-k.

factors.input_timing: shrout and cfacshr from monthlyCRSP at months t-5 and t-65 (script calendar merges L54-69; engine backward shifts of 5/65 months on the contiguous monthly template).
factors.mechanism: Identical structure to ShareIss1Y: ratio of split-adjusted shares at two strictly-past months, cumulative adjustment factor cancels except for pre-t splits; no future-month self-join on either side.

factors.input_timing: prstkc (annual Compustat) stamped at time_avail_m = datadate+6..17 months (verified CompustatAnnual.py:212-244), i.e. used only from ~6 months after fiscal year end; factor value at t uses only the row available at t.
factors.mechanism: Pointwise indicator (prstkc>0) with no time operations on either side (script ShareRepurchase.py:30-33; engine _op_positive_indicator, p1_factor_engine.py:799-800); both consume the lagged m_aCompustat stamp as-is.

factors.input_timing: monthlyCRSP vol/shrout at time_avail_m = month of observation (CRSPMonthly.py:73), available end of month t; signal at t uses vol at t, t-1, t-2 and shrout changes over t, t-1, t-2.
factors.mechanism: Script uses shift(1)/shift(2) on ascending-sorted rows (ShareVol.py:53-104); engine uses _op_lag (x.shift(n), past rows) on a complete calendar template (_op_share_volume_signal, engine:1045-1054; obs_num gate via cummax/cumsum is past-only, engine:1017-1031). All inputs are month-t-or-earlier.

factors.input_timing: Market equity of month t: script uses SignalMasterTable mve_c = shrout*|prc| of month t (CRSPMonthly.py:103); engine uses monthlyCRSP mve_permco of month t. Both are end-of-month-t values.
factors.mechanism: Pointwise log of current-month market equity, no time ops (Size.py:28; engine log(abs(mve_permco))). Engine uses permco-aggregated ME vs script's security-level mve_c — a definitional fidelity difference, not a timing one.

factors.input_timing: xrd/revt/at from m_aCompustat at datadate+6mo stamp; 12-month lag terms reference the prior fiscal year's row, available even earlier.
factors.mechanism: Script: shift(12) on ascending permno-month rows after dedup (SurpriseRD.py:26-40) — strictly past rows; engine: _op_lag(x,12) calendar shift on complete template (_op_surprise_rd_indicator, engine:1171-1185). No future alignment.

factors.input_timing: txfo/txfed/txt/txdi/ib at m_aCompustat datadate+6mo stamp; statutory top tax rate assigned by calendar year of time_avail_m — deterministic public knowledge, not data.
factors.mechanism: Pointwise ratio with piecewise fallbacks, no time operations (Tax.py:35-85; engine _op_piecewise_tax_ratio, engine:2205-2247). The rate table keyed off availability-year rather than fiscal year is a replication choice, not a leak.

factors.input_timing: All balance-sheet/cash-flow items at m_aCompustat datadate+6mo stamp; 12-month lags reach the prior fiscal year; regime switch (balance-sheet vs cash-flow method) keyed off time_avail_m year <=1989, which is deterministic.
factors.mechanism: Script shift(12) on sorted rows (TotalAccruals.py:67-95); engine .shift(12) on calendar template with identical year mask (_op_total_accruals_signal, engine:2250-2293). Trailing only.

factors.input_timing: Daily adjusted prices through the last trading day of month t (MAs A_L, TrendFactor.py:1392-1434); month-(t+1) return fRet enters only the cross-sectional beta stamped at month t; those betas are consumed with a >=1-month shift, so the newest beta used at t is _b(t-1), which requires the month-t return — realized by end of month t when the factor is stamped.
factors.mechanism: Script-backed on BOTH sides (_can_execute_natively=False; engine runs TrendFactor.py). The fRet self-join (offset_by('-1mo'), lines 1489-1499) does align row t with ret(t+1), but EBeta uses shift(1)+rolling_mean(12) over month-sorted betas (lines 1532-1540), so only _b(t-12..t-1) enter the t-stamped value — all computable from data through end of t. MA/price ratios depend only on split factors between window days and t (cfacpr ratio), known at t. NYSE-decile and price filters use month-t values. No leak.

factors.input_timing: IBES recommendations stamped time_avail_m = month of anndats (announcement date, IBESRecommendations.py:62); factor at t compares mean rec announced during month t vs the previous observed rec-month — all announced (public) by end of month t.
factors.mechanism: Script: analyst-month last rec -> firm-month mean -> groupby shift(1) lag (UpRecomm.py:29-52); engine identical, additionally sorting by anndats before taking the analyst-month last (engine:1461-1475, 2065-2084). Lag over observed months can reach further back than 1 calendar month — deeper into the past, harmless. Minor shared caveat: uses anndats rather than actdats (IBES database-entry date), the standard OSAP availability convention.

factors.input_timing: ib+dp at m_aCompustat datadate+6mo stamp; mve_permco is end-of-month-t market equity; rolling std over the trailing 60 months (min 24) ending at t.
factors.mechanism: Script asrol builds a per-permno calendar backbone and applies trailing rolling_std (VarCF.py:49-56; asrol.py:60-97, fill_date_gaps_pl is past-window only); engine rolling_std(60, min 24) on complete monthly template (_op_rolling_std, engine:779-780). Trailing only.

factors.input_timing: monthlyCRSP vol/prc/shrout of month t (available end of t); 12-month trailing mean of dollar volume ending at t, divided by month-t market equity.
factors.mechanism: Script rolling_mean(12, min 10).over(permno) trailing (VolMkt.py:48-58); engine rolling_mean(12) trailing on calendar template divided by mve_permco at t. Engine's min_obs default (6 vs script's 10) and mve_permco-vs-mve_c denominator are fidelity gaps, not timing leaks.

factors.input_timing: monthlyCRSP vol of months t-35..t (each available at its own month end); output stamped at t.
factors.mechanism: Trailing rolling_std(36, min 24) on both sides (VolSD.py:40-47; engine _op_rolling_std on complete monthly template). Past-only windows.

factors.input_timing: monthlyCRSP vol of months t-59..t feeds the trailing regression slope and 60-month mean (both clean); but the script's final trim cutoffs are the 1st/99th percentiles of VolumeTrend pooled over the ENTIRE panel — all permnos and all months, including decades after t.
factors.mechanism: Script side: VolumeTrend.py:79 calls winsor2(df, ['VolumeTrend'], replace=True, trim=True, cuts=[1,99]) with by=None; winsor2.py:122-138/162-170 then computes pl.col(var).quantile(0.01/0.99) over the full dataset and nulls observations outside those full-sample bounds — so whether a month-t value survives depends on future data (selection-only leak; surviving values are unchanged; inherited from the original Stata 'winsor2 ... trim' without by()). Engine side is clean: _op_rolling_trend_slope_scaled (engine:2584-2599) uses only the trailing 60-month window ending at t and applies no trim.

factors.input_timing: sstk, dv, prstkc, dltis, dltr, dlcch, at all from one m_aCompustat annual record: fiscal year ends at datadate, values stamped time_avail_m = datadate+6..+17 months (CompustatAnnual.py:212-244). No lags, no market data. Engine tree is the identical same-record ratio on the availability-stamped panel.
factors.mechanism: Pure within-record ratio of a single annual statement already carrying the 6-month reporting lag; no cross-time joins on either side (script XFIN.py:46-48; engine div/add/sub/fillna on m_aCompustat vars only).

factors.input_timing: oancf/ib/act/che/lct/dlc/txp/dp from m_aCompustat at t (statement public ≥6 months before t); 12-month-lagged balance-sheet items fetched via backward calendar self-merge (cfp.py:95-102, lookup key renamed so row t receives t-12); mve_permco from SignalMasterTable/monthlyCRSP at month t itself, i.e. end-of-month-t market equity used at stamp t.
factors.mechanism: All self-joins point backward and current-month ME is available by end of month t per convention. Engine side (oancf / monthlyCRSP mve_permco, same-month division) has no lags at all. Note: engine omits the script's accrual-based fallback when oancf is missing — a value discrepancy, not a timing one.

factors.input_timing: at, che, dltt, dlc, mib, pstk, ceq from m_aCompustat at t and at t-12; script lag via backward calendar merge (dNoa.py:82-93), engine lag/delta via shift(12) on the ascending availability-stamped monthly panel (p1_factor_engine.py:704-714).
factors.mechanism: Both sides difference month-t values against month t-12 values that were themselves available at t-12; denominator is lagged at. No future rows touched. Aside (non-timing): engine operating-liability leg uses derived var dc in place of the script's dlc+pstk and skips the zero-fills — a spec mismatch but same data vintage.

factors.input_timing: IBES fpi=0 meanest stamped time_avail_m = statpers month (forecast summary computed mid-month, public by month end); the value used at June t is the December t-1 forecast obtained via backward 6-month self-merge (script fgr5yrLag.py:89-98; engine p1_factor_engine.py:2436-2440, lag6_date = t-6); Compustat completeness screen at t uses m_aCompustat already lagged ≥6 months; June signal is then held forward into June..May (expansion only pushes old values to later stamps).
factors.mechanism: Lag lookup key is renamed so row t pulls the forecast issued at t-6, never the reverse; the 12-month expansion adds offsets 0..+11 so future months carry the old June value, not vice versa. Script and engine implement the same logic.

factors.input_timing: capx (and ppent for imputation) from m_aCompustat at t and t-24; annual statement public ≥6 months before its first stamped month. Script lags are position-based groupby.shift(12/24/36) on the monthly panel (ZZ1_grcapx...py:101-112) — with gaps this reaches even OLDER rows, never newer; engine uses calendar shift(24) on the full month index.
factors.mechanism: Numerator and denominator both come from statements available at or before t; FirmAge/cumcount and the ppent-based capx imputation use only prior rows. Engine omits the imputation and FirmAge screen (coverage difference, not timing).

factors.input_timing: Same file/rows as grcapx: capx at t divided by sum of capx at t-12, t-24, t-36; script position-based shifts can only reach equal-or-older calendar months, engine calendar shift(12/24/36) on the availability-stamped panel.
factors.mechanism: All three lag legs are strictly backward on both sides; the month-t capx is from a fiscal year ended ≥6 months earlier.

factors.input_timing: emp from m_aCompustat at t vs t-12; script backward calendar merge (hire.py:35-42), engine _op_hire_growth shift(12) (p1_factor_engine.py:844-847). Missing emp/lag set to 0 on both sides using only contemporaneous missingness.
factors.mechanism: Single backward 12-month lag of an already 6-month-lagged annual field; no market or cross-sectional inputs. Engine omits the year<1965 exclusion — sample-period difference only.

factors.input_timing: Ratio inputs (fatb, fatl, ppegt, ppenb, ppenls, ppent, at) from m_aCompustat at t — clean on both sides. Industry grouping differs: script uses sicCRSP from SignalMasterTable/monthlyCRSP, which CRSPMonthly.py joins from msenames with namedt<=date<=nameendt (point-in-time, known at t); engine uses m_aCompustat 'sic', which CompustatAnnual.py sources from comp.names (CCM_QUERY, line 148) — a HEADER field holding the company's latest-vintage SIC stamped identically onto every historical month.
factors.mechanism: Engine side only: _op_industry_adjusted_mean (p1_factor_engine.py:887-900) forms 2-digit industry demeaning groups at month t from the classification as of the data-download date, so a firm reclassified in, say, 2015 is demeaned against its 2015 industry peers in 1990 — future classification info leaks into historical group assignment and the >=5-obs industry screen. Script side is clean (point-in-time sicCRSP). Fix: have the engine use sicCRSP (or funda's sich, already downloaded but unused).

factors.input_timing: ibq at t where t = max(datadate+3 months, rdq month), with rdq>datadate+6mo rows dropped (CompustatQuarterly.py:83-113); atq at t-3 via backward self-merge in the script (roaq.py:44-50) and shift(3) in the engine. Stamping at the rdq month means a mid-month announcement is public before end of month t, which satisfies the stated end-of-month-t availability convention.
factors.mechanism: Both sides divide the currently-available quarter's income by assets as they were available three months earlier; all joins backward. Source-level caveats (shared, not implementation bugs): comp.fundq STD is not point-in-time so restated values can overwrite originals, and rows with missing rdq fall back to the datadate+3 assumption unverified.

factors.input_timing: IBES fpi=1 medest/numest with statpers in March, stamped time_avail_m = March (statpers is mid-March, public by month end); prc fetched at prc_time = t-3 = December of the prior year (end-of-December price used three months later — after December ends); December-FYE filter uses the datadate month of the m_aCompustat record already public at March (a statement from ~15 months earlier); coverage median split is a same-month March cross-section; signal held forward 12 months (March..February).
factors.mechanism: Script (sfe.py:29-76) and engine (_op_sfe_signal, p1_factor_engine.py:2446-2472) implement identical timing: the only cross-time joins pull the t-3 price and the already-available accounting record, and the hold-expansion only pushes the March value to later stamps. No December ME used before December; no IBES actuals involved.

factors.input_timing: vol, shrout, prc from monthlyCRSP for months t-35..t (each available at its own month end); rolling std window ends at t; size quintile/rank uses month-t market equity only. Script rolling is position-based per permno (older-only reach on gaps), engine calendar-based on the full month index.
factors.mechanism: Backward rolling window plus same-month cross-sectional size filter — nothing future-dated on either side. Aside (non-timing): engine _op_size_filtered keeps its default min_tercile=2 because the spec only passes max_quintile=3 (p1_factor_engine.py:825-841), so it also drops the bottom third by size and ranks on mve_permco, unlike the script's quintiles 1-3 on share-class mve_c — a spec-fidelity bug worth fixing separately.

factors.input_timing: che, rect, invt, ppegt, at from m_aCompustat at t (fiscal year public ≥6 months before t) — the tang value itself is clean. The manufacturing gate (2000<=sic<=3999) on BOTH sides uses m_aCompustat 'sic', which CompustatAnnual.py's CCM query (line 148) takes from comp.names — a header table whose sic is the company's most recent classification, replicated across the firm's entire history; the point-in-time sich from funda is downloaded (line 37) but never used.
factors.mechanism: Both script (tang.py:35-38 filters on m_aCompustat sic) and engine (_op_manufacturing_only on the m_aCompustat sic panel, p1_factor_engine.py:809-812) decide historical sample membership using the download-date classification: a firm that became a manufacturer in 2010 is included back to the 1970s, and one that left manufacturing is excluded from years when it genuinely qualified. The leak is in universe selection, not the computed value; same-month at-decile FC flags in the script are constructed but never applied. Fix: gate on sich or CRSP's point-in-time sicCRSP.

factors.input_timing: dailyCRSP vol/shrout stamped at trade date time_d (public at day-end); monthly aggregates (countzero, turn, ndays) for month m are complete at end of month m; factor at time_avail_m=t is the month t-1 aggregate via shift(1).
factors.mechanism: Script (ZZ1_zerotrade...py lines 57-60) stamps grouped shift(1) of the prior month's zero-volume/turnover measure, so month t uses only daily data through end of t-1; engine has no native op — zero_trade_measure is in DELEGATED_SPECIAL_OPERATORS (p1_factor_engine.py:145, 2698-2699, 2726-2730) and delegates to this same script, with standardization (lines 640-664) a pure pivot/reindex with no fills or shifts.

factors.input_timing: Same dailyCRSP vol/shrout at trade date; 6-month sums built from shift(0..5) of monthly aggregates (months m-5..m), then final shift(1) stamps the factor at t using months t-6..t-1 only.
factors.mechanism: Script lines 63-94: rolling 6-month sums of past/current monthly aggregates followed by shift(1) — value at time_avail_m=t depends solely on daily data through end of month t-1 (older across listing gaps, since shift is positional on the sorted panel — still past data); engine delegates to the identical script (DELEGATED_SPECIAL_OPERATORS, p1_factor_engine.py:145).

factors.input_timing: Same dailyCRSP vol/shrout at trade date; 12-month sums from shift(0..11) of monthly aggregates (months m-11..m), then final shift(1) stamps the factor at t using months t-12..t-1 only.
factors.mechanism: Script lines 97-146: 12-month sums of current/past monthly aggregates plus a final shift(1), so the stamped value uses only data available before month t begins; engine side is script-delegated (zero_trade_measure has no native implementation; p1_factor_engine.py:145, 2698-2730), and the CSV-to-parquet standardization introduces no time shift. Minor metadata note: the engine expression declares args (vol, ret) while the script uses (vol, shrout) — inconsequential for timing since execution delegates to the script.
